subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Movement Foundations and Safe Participation Routines
title: Performance task build: pathways, directions, and levels in combination
focus: pathways, directions, and levels in combination
essentialQuestion: What routines keep people safe and ready to move well?
materials: unit equipment listed in the guardian safety review
movementCues: Combine a pathway with a direction and a level for a richer movement.
Changes should be visible to a watcher.
Repeat combinations to make them reliable.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Combinations blur into a jog. Fix: require a watcher to name the pathway, direction, and level they saw.
keyPoints: Combine a pathway with a direction and a level for a richer movement.
Changes should be visible to a watcher.
Repeat combinations to make them reliable.
privacySafeScenario: Design and lead a warm-up, area check, and cool-down for an adult or a group, justifying each element. A learner may instead write the plan and justify it.
studentTask: The learner practises pathways, directions, and levels in combination at a self-selected challenge level, using the adapted alternative whenever it fits better, and names the cue that helped.
knowledgeCheck: The learner names one cue that helped with pathways, directions, and levels in combination and one adjustment for next time, by demonstrating, describing, drawing, or writing.
completionCriteria: The learner takes part in the task about pathways, directions, and levels in combination at a self-selected challenge level.
The learner uses or names the movement cues for pathways, directions, and levels in combination.
The learner identifies one adjustment or next step. No score, time, count, or measurement is required.
adaptationChoices: Every travel task has a seated, supported, or reduced-range version: a learner may move through space in a wheelchair or walker, travel a shorter path, use arms only, or trace the pathway with a pointer or on paper. Speed is never the target; control is. Where a task mentions a group or a partner, a learner may work with one adult instead, or plan and justify it on paper, and that counts fully.
extensionChallenge: Apply pathways, directions, and levels in combination under one new condition of the learner choosing — different equipment, space, speed, or partner — and describe what changed.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show or describe a model before practice.
Allow demonstrated, described, drawn, spoken, signed, or written evidence; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-repetition, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-stimulation options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the movement target while adjusting equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, or support.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to enjoy one safe, optional activity that practises pathways, directions, and levels in combination. No purchase, account creation, recording, measurement, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
